🔍 The Story

Step back into 1896

Innovation is booming, tensions are rising, and one shocking murder changes everything. After selling out every show last year, Death at the Silos is back! This immersive experience transforms Buffalo RiverWorks into a crime scene where you are part of the investigation.

Nikola Tesla is dazzling Buffalo with revolutionary ideas and dangerous new technology. But when a reform-minded mayor is mysteriously killed, suspicion spreads like wildfire. Was it Tesla himself, a corrupt Irish cop, a tipsy boat captain, or the madame running Buffalo’s most notorious house of ill repute?

🍽️ A Killer Menu

Your ticket includes both the immersive performance and a full buffet dinner inside the stunning Silo Events Center:

Honey Basil Chicken Breast (Gluten Free)
Beer Braised Pot Roast with Gravy
Six Cheese Bow Tie Pasta
Fresh Garden Salad
Smashed Red Potatoes
Seasonal Vegetable Medley
Warm Dinner Rolls
Coffee & Hot Tea (Fountain & Alcoholic beverages available for purchase)

🪪 $66 General Admission + fees  ·  Dinner and immersive mystery experience included  ·  Light walking and standing involved

🎟️ Get Tickets

ℹ️  Good to Know Before You Go
▼

🕵️  How does the night work?
▼

Dinner begins in the Silo Events Center. Your investigation starts the moment you walk through the doors, and after dinner guests move into the historic silos to question suspects and gather clues before returning to submit a final guess.

⚠️  What should guests expect physically?
▼

Light walking and standing are involved once the investigation moves into the silos, so guests should plan for an interactive evening rather than a seated-only show.

🍽️  Is dinner included?
▼

Yes. Your ticket includes the buffet dinner in the Silo Events Center as part of the full Death at the Silos experience.

🏆  Can you win something?
▼

Yes. Guests who correctly identify the killer can compete for prizes at the end of the night.

Grammy-winning bassist, singer, and songwriter Thundercat headlines Buffalo RiverWorks on Saturday, October 24 for a stop on the Distracted AF Tour 2026, with support from TiaCorine.

Doors open at 7:00 PM, with presale beginning 7/16 at 10 AM and public on sale starting 7/17 at 10 AM.

📖 About Distracted

We live in a time when our thumbs know more than our minds. We scroll past each other’s joy and grief before breakfast, absorb a day’s worth of tragedy by lunch, and still convince ourselves that the next notification might be the dopamine hit that’ll make us feel better. As much as some of us complain about smartphones, distraction is the air we breathe. Social media, surveillance, endless updates and countless opinions all pile up until focus feels like a luxury item. For Thundercat, the clutter isn’t abstract. On Distracted, his long-awaited fifth studio album, it’s the central theme of his life and art right now.

When asked about the album’s title, he put it simply: if you have Instagram, you already know exactly what he means. Thundercat doesn’t frame distraction as a buzzword or diagnosis. He treats it as something omnipresent, something you deal with whether you like it or not. Distracted arrives six years after It Is What It Is, an album shaped by grief, romantic heartbreak, and the loss of friend and collaborator Mac Miller. If that record felt like a long exhale after trauma, this one feels like the restless pacing that follows.

Rather than treating Distracted as a sharp turn, Thundercat sees it as continuation. The heartbreak never really stopped; it just changed shape. If it isn’t a girl, it’s taxes. If it isn’t taxes, it’s World War III. If it isn’t World War III, it’s a new update to the phone. That bleak-but-funny cadence has always been part of his voice. What’s different now is the scale of what he’s responding to.

Born Stephen Bruner in Los Angeles, Thundercat came up in a lineage built on musicianship and discipline. His father was a drummer, and his brother Ronald Bruner Jr. has played with artists ranging from Kamasi Washington to Snoop Dogg. Before Thundercat sang about love, lust, or loneliness, he learned how to listen, how to sit inside rhythm, and how to play with intention. A stint with Suicidal Tendencies sharpened his structure while widening his sonic palette.

Albums like The Golden Age of Apocalypse and Apocalypse introduced a vulnerable artist, but 2017’s Drunk crystallized Thundercat as a singular voice. Fresh off a major role on Kendrick Lamar’s landmark To Pimp a Butterfly, the emotional whiplash of Drunk mirrored the fragmented way people consume music and life in the digital age. It Is What It Is slowed that pace down and made room for grief. Distracted lives somewhere between those poles.

Thundercat insists the album wasn’t about chasing a specific sound so much as enjoying the process. That openness shines throughout the record. Songs move from layered Brit-pop influence to late-night dance-floor energy, with producer Greg Kurstin helping shape something new without forcing it. The creative throughline was not being afraid of the unknown.

That openness also extends to the album’s collaborators. Features from Willow, A$AP Rocky, Lil Yachty, and the late Mac Miller feel less like crossovers and more like conversations already in progress. The songs move through tenderness, humor, and emotional gravity without losing their weirdness or warmth.

The titles alone tell a story: I Wish I Didn’t Waste Your Time, You Left Without Saying Goodbye, She Knows Too Much. They read like internal monologues that surface at 3 a.m. when the phone is finally face down. Thundercat doesn’t over-explain them. He just calls them human sentiments, and that restraint is part of what gives the album its power.

Distracted captures the tension between overstimulation and introspection. Thundercat is skeptical of technological progress, especially the way it narrows our imagination instead of expanding it. The disappointment isn’t just about gadgets. It’s about what we were promised versus what we got.

Still, distraction isn’t always bad. Thundercat compares it to a doctor waving a toy in front of a child before a shot. Sometimes distraction helps soften the pain. Sometimes you need it to focus in a different way. That idea runs through the album and through his live show approach, where playfulness becomes part of the resistance.

If It Is What It Is was about sitting with loss, Distracted is about learning how to move again without pretending the loss didn’t happen. Thundercat’s message is simple: enjoy it, have fun, know that the struggle is real and always changing shape, and keep pushing forward.

ℹ️  Good to Know Before You Go
▼

🎧  What exactly is a silent disco?
▼

Instead of speakers, everyone dances in wireless LED headphones. Three DJs broadcast at the same time and you switch between them whenever you like, so the room is packed and loud on the headphones, and almost quiet without them.

🎫  Are headphones included with my ticket?
▼

Yes. Your ticket covers entry, all three channels of music, and a sanitized set of wireless headphones for the night. A valid ID is required for the headphone rental.

🪪  What is the age policy?
▼

This is a 21+ event. Bring a valid government-issued photo ID. It is checked at the door and again at headphone pickup.

👕  What should I wear?
▼

Wear white or neon. The room runs on UV blacklight, so light colors glow and dark colors disappear. Comfortable shoes: this is four hours of dancing.

🚗  Where do I park?
▼

Parking is available on site at Buffalo RiverWorks, 359 Ganson Street, Buffalo, NY 14203. Arrive early on winter weekends. The lot fills up.

🎉  Can I book a silent disco for my own event?
▼

Yes. SE2 Silent Disco handles party packages and headphone-only rentals. See se2.events/packages or se2.events/rentals.
